# IQ3_S paired gate/up candidate: exact scope and next qualification

Date: 2026-10-14 (JST)  
Status: source and closed-report audit only. No build, test, benchmark, model, process, environment inspection, GPU, cleanup, or Git mutation was performed. Target worktree was `feat-layer-major-bulk-upload-20261013`; selected source commit was `85cb6b1968bd5c2156eed3b10dbb332f92ee95ac` (current HEAD at review time is the later history-only merge `09cac178cb1e405686290159b1f4d766f6c712ff`). This report does not claim results on the live Main run.

## Finding

`STRATA_IQ256_PAIRED_GU=1` enables one narrow AVX2 implementation for a one-token IQ3_S gate/up projection. It shares each already-quantized Q8_K activation vector load between the gate and up row calculations. It does **not** share IQ3_S weight decoding: gate and up blocks are independently decoded, with separate integer and float accumulators. It preserves each matrix's reduction/scale order and the existing SwiGLU expression. The environment switch defaults OFF and is frozen at first use.

The closed CPU qualification (R314) reports exact float-bit parity on its synthetic fixture, in two LLVM build modes, plus an isolated NT1 synthetic mean of 0.31542 ms OFF versus 0.30355 ms ON (−3.76%). NT8 means were 0.87118 versus 0.89130 ms (+2.31%). These figures are a small, one-thread component result, not a model result. The flag remains OFF because the production count of CPU-owned `(layer, GU type=21, NT=1)` jobs is unknown and no enabled model run was recorded. R395's roughly 20% slower “paired gathering” description is ambiguous; R314 separately measures gather selection as +17.57% at NT1 and paired load-sharing as −3.76%. Do not conflate the gather variant with the paired flag or transfer either isolated result to model throughput. Both reports agree no whole-model speedup was established.

For the requested Ryzen 5 5600X, AVX2 is the relevant custom path when AVX-512 is absent. The hardware fact and local source behavior do not establish that the active10 route contains enough eligible work. The stated 982,272,000 logical GU+Down bytes/token is a logical weight-payload estimate; it is not measured DRAM traffic, CPU-owned bytes, or an estimate of this candidate's speedup.

## Exact data and dispatch contract

The source's native IQ3_S block is 110 bytes per 256 values: FP16 `d` (2 B), `qs[64]`, `qh[8]`, `signs[32]`, and `scales[4]`. The custom `Fmt32<21>` decoder handles 32-value halves. It combines low grid-index bits from `qs` with the spread high bits selected from `qh`, uses the sign bytes, and expands a packed 4-bit scale as `2*s+1`. The reference ggml layout is also defined in primary source as `d, qs, qh, signs, scales` for IQ3_S ([ggml-org/llama.cpp ggml-common.h](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/src/ggml-common.h), accessed 2026-10-14).

The candidate guard requires all of: type 21; `nt==1`; input width 2560; row width 1100; `up_off == 640*1100 == 704000`; a valid row interval within [0,640]; non-null pointers; and scalar or gather variant only. Hence each GU matrix is 640×1100 = 704,000 bytes and the packed GU region is 1,408,000 bytes. For each row, the kernel loops ten 256-value blocks and four 64-value groups, with two 32-value halves per group. It loads each 32-byte activation segment once, then separately decodes/multiplies Gate and Up. Each path accumulates integer products in the existing `maddubs`/madd-add form, converts/scales per 256-value block with FMA, horizontally reduces, and writes `silu(g)*u`. No weights or activations are converted or cached by this helper.

The public GU selector checks the exact environment value `1`, chooses the existing scalar/gather variant once, calls the paired helper, and falls back to the established GU kernel if any guard fails. On AVX2-only CPUs, `native_gu_rows` reaches the custom family only when the existing CPU dispatch is enabled and `nt >= native_gu_mt_min`; on this source, the default AVX2/no-AVX512 rule selects minimum 1 (unless the documented override/disable knobs change dispatch). AVX-512 takes precedence on capable CPUs, and `STRATA_NO_IQ256` disables this family. The paired helper itself is plain AVX2, not AVX-VNNI. Row-range arguments are passed through, so worker task splits can call it on disjoint ranges; each invocation must retain valid disjoint buffers until completion, as the header contract says. The existing direct test covers row partitions but not concurrent model-pool ownership.

Native activation quantization is upstream of this helper: IQ3_S GU input is Q8_K, and `native_quant_act` uses the AVX2 byte-identical Q8_K quantizer when enabled. SwiGLU's FF output is then quantized at the Down boundary by `native_quant_h`; for IQ4_NL Down the normal format uses its Q8_0 dot activation. This candidate changes neither activation quantizer nor Down projection. Therefore a GU bit-parity test should fix the Q8_K activation bytes; end-to-end qualification must also keep those boundary formats/quantizers identical.

## Existing fixture and what its result means

The smallest existing host fixture is `tests/core/iq3s_paired_gu_test.cpp`, registered as `iq3s_paired_gu_test` in CMake. It constructs a valid synthetic IQ3_S/IQ4_NL native layout at H=2560, FF=640, with finite FP16 block scales and deterministic packed bytes. Four activation patterns pass through the production Q8_K quantizer. For scalar and gather variants it compares all 640 candidate rows against the established GU implementation by exact float bit pattern, across row splits [0,1), [1,639), and [639,640), with canary elements. It also verifies unsupported token counts, VNNI variant, type, and range are rejected without changing output. The test is source evidence; R314 records it passed in free and contrib-LLVM builds and sanitizer qualification. This is synthetic packed weight data, not the actual model's GGUF expert tensors or model output.

Exact GU parity is the right component contract: this path exists to preserve arithmetic while reusing an activation load. A mismatch should fail, not be waved through with a tolerance. The full model has broader execution effects and should be judged with a paired production A/B: same checkpoint and hashes, prompt/token IDs, seed/sampling, provider and active10 routing, cache/residency, CPU ownership/worker/task setup, MTP/spec settings, and all math/format flags. First require the identical generated token IDs and LP5/top-logit ledger over the fixed request; any divergence is a stop-and-investigate signal, not automatic proof of unacceptable quality. Also compare per-layer route/type/NT counts and the candidate-enabled GU outputs against the baseline where observable. If exact IDs diverge despite component bit parity, capture first differing layer/token logits and quantify max absolute/relative logit error and prompt NLL on a fixed corpus before considering any tolerance. Do not replace this with a generic perplexity threshold or claim equality from a synthetic fixture. Preserve the normal no-fresh-fault, output-count, close/reap, and performance eligibility checks.

## Minimal Main-owned qualification after the current run closes

1. Use the closed request's route census or add an explicitly reviewed low-overhead request-local census to count, per layer/window, CPU-owned jobs by `(GU type, Down type, NT)`. Gate this experiment on a meaningful denominator of IQ3_S type-21, NT1 GU calls; do not infer exposure from aggregate CPU expert count or the logical bytes/token estimate.
2. On the exact production compiler/build, run the existing host parity fixture and retain its test output. Inspect generated assembly for the paired instantiation on the 5600X target to confirm no unexpected stack spills/stack traffic in the inner loop. The fixture already gives exact output and row-tail coverage; no new fixture is needed before this check. This audit did not execute either check.
3. If those gates pass, do the smallest one-axis model A/B: unset flag (OFF) versus exact `STRATA_IQ256_PAIRED_GU=1` (ON), fresh processes, interleaved order, same active10 input IDs and fixed output cap, identical saved state/cache/residency and pool setup. Keep the candidate off for other configurations. Record eligible calls/count and NT, per-call or request GU phase wall/CPU time if available, full clean request decode wall/tok/s, exact output IDs and LP5, first-divergence logits if any, and faults/normal close. Use enough paired repetitions to show a repeatable request-level delta against natural run variation; R314's two ON medians spanning 0.29594–0.31115 ms illustrate why its ~3.8% component mean alone is not promotion evidence.
4. Keep the candidate disabled unless production routing establishes material eligible work, the exact fixture and generated-code checks pass, model outputs meet the stated quality gate, and clean endpoint decode improves repeatably. A neutral or noisy result leaves default OFF.

Useful primary implementation references: local source at `src/kernels/cpu/iq_avx2.cpp` (`Fmt32<21>`, paired guard/dispatch), `src/kernels/cpu/iq_avx2_rows.inl` (paired loop), `src/kernels/cpu/native_expert.cpp` (format, quantization and dispatch), and `tests/core/iq3s_paired_gu_test.cpp`. The upstream AMD64 programmer reference documents AVX2 instruction-set support, but says nothing about this kernel's speed or spill behavior ([AMD64 Technology Programmer's Manual](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/processor-tech-docs/programmer-references/40332.pdf), accessed 2026-10-14). No external platform speed result is used.
